A_target.statement:
Let $X$ be a [[Definition:Random Variable|random variable]] and $\map S x = \map \Pr {X > x}$ its [[Definition:Survival Function|survival function]].
Then $S$ is [[Definition:Decreasing Real Function|decreasing]], [[Definition:Right-Continuous|right-continuous]], $\map S x \to 1$ as $x \to -\infty$ and $\map S x \to 0$ as $x \to \infty$.
If $X \ge 0$, then:
:$\displaystyle \expect X = \int_0^\infty \map S x \rd x$

B_source.statement:
Let $\map F x = \map \Pr {X \le x}$ be the [[Definition:Cumulative Distribution Function|distribution function]] of $X$.
Then $F$ is [[Definition:Increasing Real Function|increasing]], right-continuous, $\map F x \to 0$ as $x \to -\infty$ and $\map F x \to 1$ as $x \to \infty$.

substitutions.the event that the variable is at most x: the complementary event that it exceeds x

derived.the limits at the two ends: exchanged, so the survival function starts at one and decreases to zero
derived.the area interpretation: the integral of the survival function over the positive axis is the mean

object_map.reformulation: Replace each event by its complement, reversing every monotonicity statement while preserving continuity.

validity_conditions: Complementation of events is an order-reversing involution on probabilities, so every monotonicity statement about the distribution function reverses.
Right-continuity is preserved rather than reversed, since the complement of a right-continuous nondecreasing function is right-continuous nonincreasing.
The mean formula requires the variable to be nonnegative and integrable; for signed variables the integral must be split over the two half-lines.
proof_plan: As $F$ is increasing with limits $0$ and $1$, $S$ is decreasing with limits $1$ at $-\infty$ and $0$ at $\infty$.

If $\map F {x_n} \to \map F x$ as $x_n \downarrow x$, then $\map S {x_n} \to \map S x$.
Hence right-continuity survives the complement unchanged.
